analysis.title: Market Update US, Europe & Asia (27 October 2026)
key_insights: US equities closed higher Monday (S&P 500 +0.70%, Nasdaq +0.82%, Dow +0.28%, Russell 2000 +0.38%). The AI trade led, with semis and memory higher. Equal-weight lagged the cap-weighted index.

Meta announced a $95B equity raise ($35B common and preferred plus a $60B ATM sale of new non-voting Class C shares, expected Q1-27). SpaceX finalized a $40B debt deal with Apollo to finance Nvidia GPUs. Both helped the elevated-capex narrative that had been scrutinized the prior week.

Anthropic filed its S-1 ahead of an IPO expected as soon as the week of 9-Nov, to list on Nasdaq as 'ANT'. 1H-26 revenue rose about 1300% y/y to $16.3B. Net loss was $80.8B on non-cash valuation adjustments, while the operating loss narrowed to $693M. Top five clients are about 25% of sales and none exceeds 10%.

AMZN CEO Jassy said AWS 2026 cloud capacity is sold out, most large 2027 capacity blocks are booked and a meaningful share of 2028 is committed. Mag 7 trades at 24x P/E versus a 10-year average of about 29x, with expected EPS growth of about 34% this year versus 29% for the S&P 500.

Crude eased from multi-month highs on Mideast diplomacy headlines (WTI -1.5%), but a US strike on Iran remains possible. Trump said strikes could come imminently or after the midterms. Talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz have not produced results.
Lula defeated Flavio Bolsonaro 52%-48% in Brazil's runoff. The Bovespa ETF traded in Japan fell as much as 16% and CME FX signaled a drop of more than 10% in the real. Brazil's index fell 13.88%.

The October FOMC decision is due Wednesday at 2pm ET with a press conference by Chair Warsh. Analysts expect a hold, then a hike in December and possibly March. The key question is the statement's 'timelier return' of inflation to target. The BOC is also expected to hike Wednesday.

Strategist views are split. UBS cites a 6% average gain from end-September to end-December in midterm years. BTIG flagged a harder setup. RBC is on guard for a 5-10% S&P 500 pullback. Morgan Stanley holds an 8,000 year-end target and sees semis possibly falling another 10-15%. HSBC cut global equities from maximum overweight to neutral.
Blended Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth is 29.5%, with 83% of the 24% of companies reported beating consensus EPS.
US supply week: the $69B 2-year auction tailed by 0.3bp. $70B of 5-year notes are due Tuesday and $44B of 7-year notes Thursday. PCE and first-release Q3 GDP are due Thursday and ECI Friday.
October Dallas Fed manufacturing printed 13.4 versus 7.0 consensus and 9.8 in September.

European equities rebounded (STOXX 600 +0.8%). Moody's left France at Aa3 with a negative outlook, and the OAT-Bund spread narrowed about 13bp. The 10-year OAT had hit 5% for the first time since 2002 the prior week. JPMorgan sees about 5% of GDP in fiscal adjustment required for France.
German Ifo improved for a sixth month to 90.2 versus 89.8 consensus. UK CBI distributive trade balance was -10% versus -47% consensus.

The ECB, Fed and BoJ are all expected to hold this week, though one final 25bp ECB hike in December is the economists' base case. UK Chancellor Healey's Budget is Wednesday and is expected to raise only about £5B in taxes. ING and UBS warn the market may underestimate early UK election risk.
Asia was mixed. The Kospi fell 1.46% on a broker downgrade and the delisting of two SK Hynix leveraged funds in the US. Goldman cut its Kospi target from 12K to 9K, still about 60% upside.

Japan is seeing a rotation from AI, semis and banks into defensives and domestic demand names. Retail is up 7.5% and food up 6% this month, while electric machinery is down 8.6% and banks are down 15.2%.
The EU is planning safeguard measures (import caps or tariffs) on Chinese imports from as early as Q1-27. An agreement caps Chinese hybrid vehicle imports at 350K per year for four years.

Notable US single-stock moves: SGRY +47.6% (take-private), RRC +17.7% (EQT all-stock deal), TSLA +5.2% (Barclays upgrade), LMT +5.1% (MS upgrade), FICO -13.2% (Wells Fargo downgrade), JBLU -9.7% (creditors working with restructuring advisor), VZ -3.5% (mixed Q3).

market_movers.rationale: Barclays upgraded from equal weight, citing an M&A opportunity, a better core business outlook and signs of a Robotaxi inflection.
Morgan Stanley upgraded from equal-weight. The new F-35 deal takes significant risk out of the stock and the missile ramp is on pace.
TD Cowen upgraded from hold on valuation, improving funded backlog, federal civilian sales and price trends.
Jefferies upgraded from hold on improved visibility and financial profile versus peers. CACI also received a five-year $281M Navy task order.
UBS upgraded from neutral, seeing comp growth momentum persisting in FY27 and beyond.
Morgan Stanley downgraded from overweight on a near-term Cash App Borrow slowdown and higher credit risk, with Square facing more competition.
Wells Fargo downgraded from overweight, citing a lower-than-expected 2027 pricing announcement.
Berenberg upgraded Avio on a structural, worsening solid-rocket-motor shortage and improving visibility on US capacity.
JPMorgan downgraded Telefonica, citing high leverage at VMO2 (6x, yield-to-maturity above 15%) and refinancing and contagion risks.
Bernstein downgraded Gaztransport & Technigaz and cut its target 14%, citing overly optimistic expectations and higher French bond yields.
Prysmian resumed with buy on electrification and grid investment, the Molex deal and data-centre demand.
DNB downgraded Saab to hold after a strong Q3, saying the outlook is already priced in.
Oddo downgraded Deutsche Boerse on valuation despite a Q3 beat and raised estimates.
DNB downgraded Novonesis to hold as recent share gains leave limited upside.
Jefferies reinstated Veolia at hold on stagnant core municipal water operations and a mix shift away from higher-margin activities.

sector_views.rationale: Morgan Stanley said semiconductor shares could drop another 10-15%.
HSBC cut its global equities view from maximum overweight to neutral.
Bank of America upgraded French equities to overweight in mid-October on valuation. JPMorgan prefers non-French domestic exposure and non-French banks.
Pictet Japan sees little reason to buy defensives aggressively beyond haven trades.

earnings_insights: Blended Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth is 29.5%, with 83% of the 24% of companies that have reported beating consensus EPS.

Mag 7 EPS growth expectations are about 34% this year versus 29% for the S&P 500. Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon are expected to report double-digit quarterly revenue growth this week (Bloomberg, consensus expectations).
VZ Q3 (reported): revenue below consensus, EBITDA modestly above consensus, FCF well ahead, postpaid phone adds more than double expectations. Broadband subscribers and postpaid ARPA were weaker.
Goldman Sachs: with about 30% of MSCI Europe market cap reported, equal-weighted earnings are 1.8% above expectations. Consensus 2026 EPS growth is 21.6% (15.6% ex-Energy).
Last week's takeaways: Meta price-per-ad accelerated, SpaceX raised its 2027 compute target to 13GW+ from about 10GW, and Lam Research guided preliminary 2027 WFE above $200B (+30%), led by DRAM.
Computacenter raised FY2026 adjusted pre-tax profit guidance to not less than £425M from £380M, versus company-compiled consensus of £387.1M.
Deutsche Boerse Q3 reported: revenue EUR1.633B, EBITDA EUR978M, EPS EUR3.10, all above consensus. FY26 EBITDA guidance raised to about EUR3.9B.
Gaztransport & Technigaz 9-month revenue was EUR570M versus EUR581M consensus. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed.
Galp Q3 beat consensus on EBITDA, EBIT and net income and raised FY2026 EBITDA and CFFO guidance.
Saab Q3 reported: organic sales +31%, EBIT +42%, order intake 12% above consensus, operating cash flow SEK 6.8B.

Hisense Home Appliances Q3 revenue was CNY20.25B versus CNY22.01B estimate. HD Hyundai Marine Solution Q3 operating profit was KRW95.7B versus KRW106.88B estimate. BNK Financial Q3 operating profit was KRW239.49B versus KRW303.43B estimate.
Infosys cut its FY27 revenue growth forecast on AI-driven pricing pressure and sluggish demand. FANUC raised FY guidance and announced a buyback of up to 50B yen.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Above the 7.0 consensus and September's 9.8, with slower output growth, improved perceptions of conditions and price pressures edging higher.
Consensus expectation that the actual print beat.

crypto_views: Two SK Hynix leveraged funds are to be delisted in the US amid the cooling AI rally.
risk_factors: AI capex financing strain: tightening debt markets (Musk comments), the SpaceX CDS record, and Meta's $95B raise that includes ATM share sales.
Renewed US military action against Iran and disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, keeping oil elevated.
FOMC statement language and a December hike that markets expect.
French fiscal and political risk: OAT-Bund spread at a 15-year high, with contagion to Belgium.
Brazil political uncertainty after the narrow Lula win and Bolsonaro's call for annulment.
An S&P 500 pullback of 5-10% (RBC) and a further 10-15% drop in semiconductors (Morgan Stanley).
Regulatory headwinds facing data center construction, which weaken the case for taking hyperscaler cash-flow consensus at face value (Nikkei).
UK early-election risk affecting sterling and gilts.
Korea: slowing earnings revision momentum, completed corporate buybacks, foreign outflows and a two-year-high won.
vol_and_positioning: The volatility index closed at 18.39, down 5.45% on the day and up 12.55% month to date.
Recent hedge-fund derisking and CTA short covering were cited as supports, along with a setup for a potential momentum bounce.
The post-election slide in Brazil and a potential relief rally after next week's US midterms were also noted.
In Japan, low margin ratios of 0-3% in recent defensive winners (ZOZO, OLC) indicate relatively high short positions and potential short-covering, versus SoftBank at 10 and Kioxia at 25.
Pictet Japan warned that continued weakness in AI, semis and banks could increase unrealized losses and lead to margin calls.
SpaceX CDS hit a record 266bp on Friday on investor concerns over AI-related capex.
geopolitical: Middle East: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey officials were to meet Iranian officials to push an interim deal reopening the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for lifting blockades on Iran's ports and releasing frozen assets. Trump said strikes could come imminently or after the midterms. CNN reported US forces could launch major operations within 96 hours of an order. Iran threatened civilian, energy and AI-related targets across the Middle East if attacked.
Brazil: Lula won the runoff 52%-48% over Flavio Bolsonaro, who called for an annulment.

EU-China trade: Brussels plans safeguard measures on Chinese imports and agreed a 350K per year cap on Chinese hybrid vehicles. China's commerce ministry warned the EU not to underestimate its resolve. Beijing 'firmly opposed' a US proposal to tighten investment limits.
Ukraine: European governments seek a stronger role in peace negotiations as Washington engages Moscow. The EU is preparing to cover about EUR46.7B of Ukraine's additional EUR70B funding request.
France: fragmented parliament and Apr-Jun 2027 elections limit deficit reduction. A far-right versus far-left runoff is JPMorgan's base case.
UK: ING and UBS warn the market may underestimate early election risk.
US-Canada: the two countries are working on a deal to ease US tariffs on Canadian steel and auto imports (Reuters).
cross_bank_references: UBS noted the S&P 500 has averaged a 6% gain from end-September to end-December in midterm years, while BTIG flagged a more difficult setup.
JPMorgan expects contagion from French bond stress to be limited, while Bank of America upgraded French equities to overweight in mid-October.
Goldman Sachs cut its Kospi target while JP Morgan highlighted fading corporate buyback support.
ING and UBS both warned the market may be underestimating UK early-election risk.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS notes the S&P 500 has averaged a 6% gain from end-September to end-December in midterm years. Morgan Stanley holds an 8,000 year-end target, and a relief rally is possible after the midterms.
tension_points.bear_case: BTIG flags a more difficult setup. RBC is on guard for a 5-10% pullback, Morgan Stanley sees semis falling another 10-15%, and HSBC cut equities to neutral.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 5-10% S&P 500 pullback (RBC) or a further 10-15% drop in semiconductor shares (Morgan Stanley) would undercut the bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: Moody's left France at Aa3 with a negative outlook. Bank of America upgraded French equities to overweight on valuation, and the CAC 40 trades at a record-low relative P/E.
tension_points.bear_case: The 10-year OAT passed 5% and the spread to Bund is at a 15-year high, with Belgian contagion. JPMorgan sees about 5% of GDP in required fiscal adjustment, and the 2027 budget's EUR43B of measures faces slippage risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Political clarity would close the roughly 55bp excess in the OAT-Bund spread. A far-right versus far-left runoff in the 2027 election is JPMorgan's base case.

tension_points.bull_case: Meta's raise and the SpaceX debt deal support the elevated-capex narrative. AWS capacity is sold out through much of 2027 and hyperscaler cash flow is forecast to outpace investment after 2026/27.
tension_points.bear_case: SpaceX CDS hit a record, debt markets are tightening (Musk), and Nikkei cautions against taking street expectations at face value given regulatory headwinds for data centers.
